Method of Attack: Bypassing authentication procedures by exploiting incorrect handling of password retries in boot scripts, allowing an attacker to hold Enter key for ~70 seconds to open a root shell
Repeated password retries reload authentication procedure up to 93 times on x86 and 452 times on PowerPC
After exhausting password attempts, an Initrd shell with root privileges is opened
Elevation of privilege via storing SetUID executables on unencrypted boot partition
Information disclosure by accessing and copying encrypted system partition for offline brute forcing
Denial of service by deleting disk information
Impacted Systems: Linux distributions based on Debian (e.g., Ubuntu)
Fedora (using Dracut instead of initramfs, e.g., Fedora 24 x86_64)
Attack Vector: Physical access to affected device to trigger boot and exploit authentication bypass
Remote exploitation possible on cloud-based Linux systems
